**Setting up.** Let $\Phi(N)=\sum_{n\le N}\phi(n)$. Using $\sum_{d\mid n}\phi(d)=n$ and summing over $n\le N$ gives the identity

$$\sum_{k=1}^{N}\Phi\!\left(\lfloor N/k\rfloor\right)=\frac{N(N+1)}{2},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \Phi(N)=\frac{N(N+1)}{2}-\sum_{k=2}^{N}\Phi\!\left(\lfloor N/k\rfloor\right).$$

To evaluate $\Phi(2026)$ I need $\Phi$ at all values $\lfloor 2026/k\rfloor$, i.e. at $1,\dots,45$ and at $46,47,48,49,50,51,53,54,56,57,59,61,63,65,67,69,72,75,77,81,84,88,92,96,101,106,112,119,126,135,144,155,168,184,202,225,253,289,337,405,506,675,1013$.

**Direct table.** I computed $\phi(n)$ for $n\le 506$ and accumulated, obtaining (among others):

$\Phi(100)=3044,\ \Phi(200)=12232,\ \Phi(253)=19566,\ \Phi(289)=25526,\ \Phi(337)=34678,\ \Phi(405)=49986,\ \Phi(506)=77964$,

and smaller needed values such as $\Phi(184)=10340,\ \Phi(168)=8610,\ \Phi(155)=7356,\ \Phi(144)=6330,\ \Phi(135)=5570,\ \Phi(126)=4832,\ \Phi(119)=4354,\ \Phi(112)=3836,\ \Phi(106)=3426,\ \Phi(101)=3144,\ \Phi(96)=2806,\ \Phi(92)=2596,\ \Phi(88)=2368,\ \Phi(84)=2166,\ \Phi(81)=2020,\dots$

Each of $\Phi(200),\Phi(253),\Phi(289),\Phi(337),\Phi(405),\Phi(506)$ was verified independently by the recursion formula above, and all agreed.

**Larger values via recursion.**

- $\Phi(675)=\dfrac{675\cdot676}{2}-89464=228150-89464=138686$ (also confirmed by directly summing $\phi(507),\dots,\phi(675)=60722$ and adding to $\Phi(506)$).
- $\Phi(1013)=\dfrac{1013\cdot1014}{2}-201133=513591-201133=312458$ (consistent with the known $\Phi(1000)=304192$ plus $\sum_{1001}^{1013}\phi(n)=8266$).

**Final step.** $T(2026)=\dfrac{2026\cdot2027}{2}=2053351$. The sum $\sum_{k=2}^{2026}\Phi(\lfloor 2026/k\rfloor)$ consists of the individual terms for $k=2,\dots,77$:

$312458+138686+77964+49986+34678+25526+19566+15428+12464+10340+8610+7356+6330+5570+4832+4354+3836+3426+3144+2806+2596+2368+2166+2020+1832+1736+1588+1470+1394+1308+1228+1162+1086+1000+964+900+882+806+774+754+712+696+650+628+604+584+542+530+490+474+2\cdot450+432+2\cdot396+384+2\cdot360+2\cdot344+2\cdot324+2\cdot308+2\cdot278+2\cdot270+3\cdot242+3\cdot230+2\cdot212$

plus the grouped tail $4\cdot200+3\cdot180+4\cdot172+4\cdot150+4\cdot140+5\cdot128+5\cdot120+6\cdot102+7\cdot96+7\cdot80+9\cdot72+9\cdot64+11\cdot58+13\cdot46+16\cdot42+18\cdot32+23\cdot28+28\cdot22+36\cdot18+48\cdot12+68\cdot10+101\cdot6+169\cdot4+338\cdot2+1013\cdot1$.

(The multiplicities total $2025$, as required.) Adding carefully (and re-adding in a different grouping as a check) gives the sum $805535$.

Therefore
$$\Phi(2026)=2053351-805535=1247816.$$

Sanity check: $3\cdot2026^2/\pi^2\approx 1247672$, and our value exceeds it by about $144$, a reasonable error-term size.

ANSWER: 1247816
